title: Hairpin lace bookmark
excerpt: A quick narrow bookmark in lace weight yarn worked on a hairpin lace frame. A single strip with knotted fringe at each end makes a delicate, practical gift.
sourceNotes: A single narrow hairpin lace strip with the side loops left open and finished with a simple fringe at each end.
aliases: hairpin lace book marker lace weight

glossaryTerms.definition: Short lengths of yarn folded and looped through the end loops of a strip, then secured with an overhand knot close to the edge.
The single double crochet worked in the centre of the hairpin frame on every pass to build the backbone of the strip.

crochet.gaugeText: Each strip = 2 cm wide with prongs set 2 cm apart.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 2 cm wide x 20 cm long (excluding fringe).

content.text: The bookmark is a single hairpin lace strip built around a central

Set the frame to 2 cm. Slip the starting loop onto the left prong and chain 1. Work 1 double crochet in the centre, rotate the frame, and repeat. Continue until 40 loops sit on each side. Remove carefully from the frame.

Cut 6 lengths of yarn, each 10 cm long. Fold 3 lengths together, loop them through the end loops at one end, and tie a knot close to the edge. Repeat at the other end. Trim the fringe evenly. Weave in the remaining ends with the tapestry needle.
